newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi urges women to veil, be "properly covered".
newsitem.headline: Saudi urges women to veil, be "properly covered".

text.p: Saudi Arabia is urging citizens to ensure women do not leave their homes without being veiled and "properly covered", the daily Saudi Gazette said on Tuesday.

A Ministry of Information statement carried by the paper said "religious scholars and educated people should organise lectures and meetings to point out the negative effects of allowing women to go to the market or roam about without being properly covered".

"According to Islamic teachings, the fathers, husbands and guardians are responsible for the care of their families. They should not allow their women to go out without being veiled and unprotected," the newspaper said.

In Saudi Arabia, women must cover their hair in public and wear the long-sleeved black "abaya" cloak. When they leave their homes they should be accompanied by their "mahram" -- a close male relative such as their husband, father, or adult son. Women are also forbidden to drive.
Some women in the conservative Islamic kingdom wear full facial veils which do not even leave slits for the eyes.
